emulators.name: RetroArch
emulators.notes: A frontend for emulators, game engines, and media players that uses the libretro API as its modular backbone.

emulators.name: DuckStation
emulators.notes: A source-available PlayStation emulator developed primarily by stenzek, featuring PGXP, upscaling, texture filtering, and run-ahead support.

emulators.name: PCSX2
emulators.notes: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 emulator for Windows, Linux, and macOS supporting a high level of compatibility.

emulators.name: RPCS3
emulators.notes: An open-source PlayStation 3 emulator and debugger written in C++ for Windows, Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD.

emulators.name: shadPS4
emulators.notes: A free and open-source PlayStation 4 emulator written in C++ supporting Windows, Linux, and macOS.

emulators.name: KytyPS5
emulators.notes: An experimental emulator for running PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 software and homebrew.

emulators.name: AnyPS5
emulators.notes: A conceptual repository targeting native-port layering for PlayStation 5 architecture.

emulators.name: PPSSPP
emulators.notes: An open-source PSP emulator that allows users to play PlayStation Portable games in high definition on multiple platforms.

emulators.name: Vita3K
emulators.notes: The first functional experimental PlayStation Vita emulator and debugger for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

emulators.name: Dolphin
emulators.notes: An open-source emulator for GameCube and Wii games that supports high-definition rendering, network play, and modding tools.

emulators.name: Cemu
emulators.notes: An open-source Wii U video game console emulator compatible with Windows and Linux operating systems.

emulators.name: Ryujinx (Ryubing)
emulators.notes: Ryubing, the maintained Ryujinx. Its site moved from GitLab to Forgejo. An open-source Nintendo Switch emulator focused on accuracy, performance, and a user-friendly interface.

emulators.name: Eden
emulators.notes: A community-focused Nintendo Switch emulator branch derived from the broader ecosystem.

emulators.name: Sudachi
emulators.notes: An experimental Nintendo Switch emulator fork based on the Yuzu architecture.

emulators.name: Eglantine
emulators.notes: An experimental emulator project combining codebases from Eden, Yuzu, and Sudachi architectures.

emulators.name: Lichii
emulators.notes: A very experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator (it also runs Switch titles), forked from Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi. Early builds are Windows-only pre-releases, so expect crashes and rendering errors.

emulators.name: Azahar
emulators.notes: A Nintendo 3DS emulator that acts as a direct continuation and successor to Lime3DS and Citra architectures.

emulators.name: melonDS
emulators.notes: A fast and accurate Nintendo DS and DSi emulator supporting local Wi-Fi multiplayer and OpenGL rendering.

emulators.name: mGBA
emulators.notes: An emulator for running Game Boy Advance games with a focus on speed, accuracy, and low hardware requirements.

emulators.name: Rosalie's Mupen GUI
emulators.notes: A graphical user interface for Mupen64Plus written in C++ using Qt, focused on a modern desktop experience.

emulators.name: Mesen2
emulators.notes: A multi-system emulator built for high accuracy, deep debugging features, and broad retro platform compatibility.

emulators.name: Xenia Canary
emulators.notes: An experimental build branch of the Xenia Xbox 360 emulator incorporating early fixes and features.

emulators.name: xemu
emulators.notes: An open-source original Xbox emulator enabling users to run commercial dashboard and game software on modern hardware.

emulators.name: Flycast
emulators.notes: A multi-platform Sega Dreamcast, Naomi, and Atomiswave emulator derived from Reicast.

emulators.name: Ymir
emulators.notes: An emulator designed to target and run Sega Saturn software titles.

emulators.name: BigPEmu
emulators.notes: A high-performance emulator and development tool for the Atari Jaguar and Atari Jaguar CD systems.

emulators.name: MAME
emulators.notes: An extensive multi-purpose hardware preservation project designed to reproduce arcade machines and vintage computers.

emulators.name: ares
emulators.notes: An open-source multi-system emulator focused on cycle accuracy and source code clarity.

emulators.name: Snes9x
emulators.notes: A portable Super Nintendo Entertainment System (TM) emulator.

emulators.name: Project64
emulators.notes: A free and open-source emulator for the Nintendo 64 and Nintendo 64 Disk Drive.

emulators.name: Lime3DS
emulators.notes: A Nintendo 3DS emulator based on Citra.

emulators.name: FinalBurn Neo
emulators.notes: A multi-system arcade emulator designed for retro gaming enthusiasts.

emulators.name: DOSBox Staging
emulators.notes: A modern continuation of DOSBox with advanced features and current development practices.

emulators.name: ScummVM
emulators.notes: Allows you to play classic graphic point-and-click adventure games.

emulators.name: BlastEm
emulators.notes: An open source, highly accurate emulator for the Genesis/Megadrive that runs on modest hardware.

emulators.name: BlueStacks
emulators.notes: A popular Android emulator for running mobile games and apps on desktop. Windows only, and it comes only as an installer: Distill downloads it, checks it against its published SHA-256, and you run it to install.
